venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Saturday 11/21 (MOD JK; entered by Mya; posted 3:07am ET 11/22)** Net $6,899 vs target $8,535 (80.8%). Food $275; no events; comps $65.10 (0.9%). 230 guests; check avg $30.00. Holidays are approaching, but flow picked up compared to Friday. Opener came in with a mid and two closers, and the opener was still able to leave around 8pm. A lot more regulars in tonight; lots of guests mentioned upcoming travel plans, which will affect the rest of the week. Coaching note: keep getting out from behind the bar — the more the team ABKs the space, the fewer broken glasses to deal with. A wedding party came in to close the night. Kitchen: smooth night. No events. Maintenance: keeping an eye on the dishwasher — a follow-up post in the channel (4:17am ET) says it is still spraying and was having a hard time cleaning beer mugs. 86 shorty service. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Highlight: seeing regulars who had moved out of town back in town for the holidays.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Saturday 11/21 (MOD Morgan, Chef Amanda; entered by BT; posted 3:46am ET 11/22)** Net $12,612 vs target $11,485 (109.8%). Food $499; no events; comps $198 (1.6%). 383 guests; check avg $33. A pretty decent night from start to finish. It began with a birthday party of approximately 30 people, which got sales up to $2,000 by 7pm. Steady until around 10:30pm, when the first pop hit and persisted until about 1am; some folks hung out until 1:30 and a handful of regulars stayed until 2. The DJ killed it — guests were on the dance floor. Kitchen: smooth sailing; Amanda held it down. 86 ponies. No events; no maintenance needs; no incidents; no-shows not charged. Highlight: a regular came in to celebrate her new job at a law firm after years of working toward it.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Saturday 11/21 (AM MOD Maggie H, Chef Lucas; PM MOD Evan F; entered by Evan F; posted 4:05am ET 11/22)** Net $31,070.05 incl. events; daily target entered as '???' on the form, so no target recorded. AM (coffee) $1,882.66, D&C PM $13,749.89, Garden/6A n/a; net before events $15,632.55; net event sales $15,437.50 (event food $6,650.00). Food incl. events $9,972.95 (food before events $3,322.95). Comps $356.39 (~2.59%). 389 guests (Tock); check avg $79.87 (net incl. events / guests). AM: no report for 11/21. PM: good night — busy from 6pm with an event in house and a constant flow of people; big numbers even with being down a server. Everyone crushed it despite dealing with tough guests all night. Kitchen: steady night with a busy pop; Lucas and Rand knocked out the wedding. Emma thanked the team for their patience since her injury. Event: wedding ceremony/reception with 50 guests, 5pm–10pm in the Garden/Vauxhall. Weather was a little crisp and the ceremony was lovely; the family-style dinner went smoothly and the event team crushed it while down a server. The wedding planner and the couple thanked the team on leaving. Break make-up complete. No incidents; no-shows not charged. Maintenance: service well swing-door freezer was not holding temp throughout service. Highlight: seeing friends from home in the room.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Saturday 11/21 (MOD Kyler, Chef Steves; entered by Thomas; posted 3:12am ET 11/22; date field typed '11//21')** Net $8,254 vs target $8,003 (103.1%). Food $1,030, beverage $7,224; retail $240 (reported separately — food + beverage = net); no event sales. Comps $271.34 (3.3%) — community member, community member gifts, and service recovery making up more than 50%. 219 guests (SevenRooms); check avg $37.69 (net/guests; form $38). The open was crimped by an excess of 6:30/6:45/7:15 reservations, but the bar opened to a massive line and was full until 12:30, aside from the middle booths, which were a bit disappointing. Good team effort. 219 covers, 2 large parties, 8 solos, 8 investor cocktails. Top sellers: Native Lion, Rosalie, Large Space, Shinebox. Kitchen: an insane amount of snacks in the final hours. Door: another really nice night outside; started with a semi-full room but a waitlist right away, stayed full until about 11 and kept the waitlist all night. Folks were moody at the door, but some sweet guests lifted the vibes; visits from regulars and friends from Amor y Amargo at the end of the night. Two no-shows (a 2-top at 7:30 and a 4-top at 10); no-shows not charged. Menu count 18. Breakage: 1 DOF.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Saturday 11/21 (MOD Julian, Chef Saleh; entered by Julian Catano; posted 6:14am ET 11/22)** Net $14,314 vs target $13,421 (106.7%). Marquee $10,464 (food $1,750); Standing Room $3,850 (food $712). Food $2,462; no events. Comps $477.94 (3.3%; gifts, comps, DNLs, discounts). 382 guests; check avg $37.47 as reported. Guests were waiting outside at 6pm before open, and the night stayed constant and busy throughout — as soon as one table closed out it was cleaned, reset and ready for the next. A handful of large parties kept the team busy. Good flow of guests entering, with a healthy waitlist; the team accommodated almost everyone who chose to wait, right up to last call. Overall a very busy shift. Kitchen: all hands on deck with food flying out of the pass. Maintenance: oven still down. 86: french fries. No incidents; no-shows charged. Highlight: being on the floor helping the team in any way possible.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative: **DC — Saturday 11/21 (MOD Josh / Jesse; entered by Jesse; posted 3:31am ET 11/22)** Net $9,815.54 incl. events vs target $9,560 (102.7%). Marquee bar $8,034.54; Garden $1,781.00 (the two sum to the net figure); 'Total Sales' entered as $12,852.80. Food $658.80; no events. Comps reported as 3.0% with no dollar amount (largely the usual, plus one walk-out related to an incident with an intoxicated individual — detailed report already sent to Josh and Marcus); voids 0.7% (86'd items, entry errors). 228 guests (69 reservations, 159 walk-ins); guest avg $37.90 and check avg $83.17 as reported. Garden: pretty quiet start, kicked off around 8:30 and settled into a really nice flow; a mix of larger parties, waitlisted folks and people enjoying the ambiance and warmer weather. Jada and Owen crushed it with great comms and teamwork, rotating between taking orders and making drinks; the host team did a good job bussing and flipping the space. D&C: slower start with a few larger tables; really picked up around 8:30pm, with the room filling completely and a waitlist started. Service ran pretty smoothly with solid communication. A small lull of about 30 minutes, then the room filled back up around 11:30pm with a waitlist again for a bit at the end. Being down a barback was a wrinkle early; the MODs floated in to help with glassware until Sasha was moved behind the bar, since the floor had ample hands with Michael training. Bar top stayed steady and the bar team passed tickets well to stay ahead of ticket times. Floor service was pretty solid but has room to improve on attentiveness and table maintenance — coaster drops, water service and pre-bussing need more intention. A good Saturday with the holiday approaching. Kitchen: very slow night; James and Rasaan used the down time to run food and support the floor. Went well: teamwork, pacing, regulars. Do better: coaster drops, water service, pre-bussing. The form's incident field says No, though the comp notes reference the intoxicated-guest walk-out. No-shows not charged; no-show revenue $0. Maintenance: hot water, curtain. Highlight: the Keany delivery driver finally bringing his family in for a drink.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.weather: pretty bad! Cool, damp and rainy all day long
venues.narrative: **MG — Saturday 11/21 (AM MOD James, Chef Marcus; PM MOD Sam, Chef Shannon; entered by Alexis; posted 1:47am ET 11/22)** Net $13,169 vs target $13,967 (94.3%). Municipal Bar AM $3,570, PM $7,801; Hot Eye $1,678; Sun Club closed ($0). Food $4,380; no events; comps $181 (1.4%). 321 guests (OpenTable: 102 AM + 219 PM); check avg $41.03 (net/guests). Weather: cool, damp and rainy all day. AM: a steady Saturday morning by the numbers, and busy considering the weather across the Southeast — the guests who made it in were ready to drink. Slow start, then a few really decent hours in the middle. PM: a mellow Saturday with the rain scaring people away. Started with 50-something on the books; busiest hour was 6–7pm with a solid push from the concert that started at 7:30, then slowly petered out. No SA tonight, so the team fell a bit behind on sidework, but the two hosts did a great job helping bus and reset tables. Four servers was right for the volume; not many large parties, which kept things tight. Hot Eye: very slow — a decent opening hour before the show, then it tapered off quickly; only a handful of guests until around 11pm, then one really busy hour. Some industry guests came in for burritos, but none were in the hotbox and it hadn't been communicated that they were never made, so those guests left. Kitchen: no DNLs or send-backs; kept pace well with business; no lows or 86s; focusing on Thanksgiving Day prep for the rest of the week. No events; no incidents. Highlight: selling a few Conferences, which were a total hit.

venues.name: D&C Seattle
venues.weather: Highs around 50, lows high 30s. Misty rain on and off all day with foggy skies.
venues.narrative: **SEA — Saturday 11/21 (MOD Curtis; entered by Frank; posted 4:45am ET 11/22)** Net $11,044 vs target $11,492 (96.1%). Food $1,345; no events; comps $299.84 (2.7%; a few members/investors, lots of F&F, and a few more DNLs than usual). 245 guests; check avg $45.07. Highs around 50 and lows in the high 30s, with misty rain on and off and foggy skies — people still came out. A Huskies game and a Kraken game made for a slow start that picked up into a decently steady service. The main rush started a bit earlier than normal and there wasn't as much of a pre-dinner drop-off as usual. Lots of friends and industry folks came through — between 7 and 11pm there were always one or two friends/family at the bar. The last hour was nice and busy, with a few surprise parties getting in for one before close. Everyone on the floor and bar broke smoothly and got staff meal. Staggered in-times continue to work well, and weekend cuts have been smooth. Kitchen: decently mellow night compared to the usual flow; staff meal was a hit. No events. Maintenance (urgent): the toilet in the bathroom closest to the office isn't flushing — needs someone in ASAP. 86: Awayuki Strawberry gin, Monkey 47. Low: Cointreau (all in cheaters), Hendrick's, Hampden Estate, Romate Fino, Daiyame 25, Taittinger Brut, Heart of Stone Sour. No incidents; no-shows charged. Highlight: all the industry folks who came through — from brand owners to neighborhood bartenders — it felt more like a Sunday than a Saturday.
